Commentary.Commentary: That's all we have from this game. This series is done and dusted in favour of New Zealand but there is still one game to go. Do join us on Friday, 15th July 2022, for the third ODI in Dublin. The match will begin at 3.15 pm IST (9.45 am GMT) but you can join us in advance for the build-up. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Tom Latham, the skipper of New Zealand, says that he is happy with the performance and feels that winning the toss was important. Praises his bowlers for providing such a fantastic start and getting a couple of early wickets to set the tone. Also adds that the spinners were brilliant. He admits that it was a shaky start from their batters but they gradually got the grip of the game and managed to build some partnerships which ultimately helped them to get over the finish line. Tells that the way Finn Allen played was a big positive and Michael Bracewell once again showed his composure to finish things off. Hopes that he continues his good form.

The Irish skipper, Andy Balbirnie says that the pitch was tricky with the ball nipping around and then turning as well. Adds that they did well afterwards but it wasn't enough. Mentions they bowled well but will look to improve as well. Adds that George Dockrell batted beautifully and can hit the ball really well and Andy McBrine was also solid at the top. Tells that they could be better in the field and there were some positives for them but they have to improve.

Michael Bracewell is picked for the Player of the Match award. 10-1-26-2 with the ball and an unbeaten 42 runs with the bat - It was an incredible all-round show by him. He says that the bowlers did an excellent job at the start and bowling three maidens set the tone for the game. Praises Jacob Duffy for his debut. Shares that the pitch was offering spin and they used the conditions well. He is happy with the way they restricted Ireland to a low score. He sounds satisfied to take New Zealand over the line.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

Earlier in the match, Tom Latham won a crucial toss and decided to bowl under overcast conditions. The Irish batters found it tough to deal with the seaming deliveries and soon were found struggling. It was George Dockrell's knock and the late cameo from Mark Adair that handed them runs on the board to fight with, but 216 was never going to be enough against a team like New Zealand. In hindsight, the 12 balls that Ireland wasted could have made the difference.

It was a shocking start for New Zealand as they lost two wickets off the first two balls of the chase. Mark Adair was exceptional in his first few overs and pegged the Kiwis back fairly early. The going was tough, but Finn Allen and Tom Latham applied themselves to soak all the pressure. The former cut loose after that to steal the momentum in New Zealand's favour. This pair put together a century stand to corner the Irish team. Latham dropped into the role of the anchor and the likes of Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips also added vital runs.

Slight hiccup for the Black Caps, but eventually, they ended up securing an unassailable lead in the series, along with the crucial Super League points. Michael Bracewell once again played a mature knock and made sure that New Zealand cross the line.

SIX! BANG! Michael Bracewell finishes things off in style! Simi Singh angles it into the pads, Bracewell dances down the track and gives himself a bit of room before lifting it over the long on fence for a maximum. New Zealand win by 3 wickets!
On a good length, angling into the body. Bracewell shuffles a bit and works it towards mid-wicket for one.

FIVE WIDES! A wild delivery from Little, a gift really. Little tries to bowl a yorker at the toes but the ball slips out of his hands and end up being a high full toss, way down the leg side. The ball eludes the batter and the diving keeper to race away into the fine leg fence. New Zealand are a hit away now from victory!

APPEAL! Not given. Josh Little goes fuller and angles it in from around off. Michael Bracewell shuffles across looks to punch it back past the bowler but misses and the ball flicks the pads on its way to the keeper. Huge appeal from the bowler but it is turned down! Not sure whether they are claiming a catch or going up for lbw but it is being checked. UltraEdge is checked first and there is a flat line as the ball passes the bat and the Ball Tracking shows that the impact is well outside off.
Back of a length and on off, Michael Bracewell defends it off the back foot.
On a fullish length and pushed a bit wider, Henry looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge that flies through the vacant backward point region. They get a single.
This is full and wide, Matt Henry looks to take it down but misses the ball completely.
Back of a length and around off, Henry rocks back and has a tentative push at it past the man at point for a couple of runs.

SIX! Michael Bracewell punishes Singh for his error and New Zealand inche closer to the target. Tossed up again around middle. Bracewell clears his front leg and heaves it over mid-wicket for a maximum.

No ball! Oh, dear! Simi Singh commits the cardinal sin and this will hurt Ireland with only a few runs left to defend. This is flighted and around off, Michael Bracewell pushes it out towards cover. Singh has overstepped and it will be a Free Hit!
Quicker and flatter, around off. Bracewell taps it towards point.
Matt Henry arrives. He has a word with Michael Bracewell before taking guard. 20 needed more. 3 wickets left. New Zealand have needlessly made it close.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mitchell Santner holes out and provides a lifeline to Ireland! This is tossed up again by Simi Singh, around middle and leg. Santner dances down the track and looks to flick it aerially over the mid-wicket fence but ends up lifting it high and straight to the fielder. Curtis Campher settles under it and takes a comfortable catch in the deep. Suddenly, New Zealand are 7 down with 20 runs still left to get.
Commentary.Howout: c Curtis Campher b Simi Singh

Commentary.Commentary: This is angled into middle and leg, Santner blocks it out.
Nicely bowled! Drifting into off, on a length and just turning away a touch. Mitchell Santner tries to block off the front foot but misses and gets hit high on the back leg.
Full and straight, firmly pushed back towards the bowler who misfields and the ball goes towards long on. The batters get across for a single.
Pulls his length back a bit, on middle, Mitchell Santner knocks it to mid on.
Goes full again down the leg side, Michael Bracewell flicks it off his pads through square leg for a run.
Good length on off, Michael Bracewell defends it down the pitch.
Lands this one short on middle and off, Michael Bracewell tries to pull it but mistimes it. The ball takes the bottom edge and falls close to the stumps.
Full and on middle and leg, Mitchell Santner drives it towards mid on and gets across for a quick single.
Serves it full, drifting into the pads. Michael Bracewell helps it towards fine leg for a single.
Josh Little is back into the attack.
Around middle, Santner defends it off the front foot.
Bracewell tries to repeat the trick but Singh pulls back the length. Bracewell adjusts well and nudges it past square leg for a single.
SIX! Shot of a man full of confidence! Tossed up on a length and around off, Michael Bracewell steps out and just lifts it high and handsome over the long on fence for a biggie.
Quicker this time, on off. Michael Bracewell manages to keep it out.
Full and on the pads, this is nudged away towards square leg.
Nicely drifting into middle, Santner looks to defend but gets an inside edge towards square leg. The batters sneak in a quick run.
A bit short outside off, Michael Bracewell flicks it straight to mid-wicket.
Full and on middle and off, Michael Bracewell is solid in his defense.

Appeal for a catch, not given. This is tossed up on middle, drifting away. Michael Bracewell uses his feet but misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads to the second slip fielder. They appeal for the catch but the umpire is not interested.
Slower through the air on off, turning away. Michael Bracewell blocks it to the off side.
Tossed up on middle, Michael Bracewell pushes it to mid on.
FOUR! Brilliant shot! This is full on off, Michael Bracewell comes down the pitch and smashes it over mid on for a boundary.
On a shorter length and around middle and leg, Santner defends it out.
FOUR! No messing around from Mitchell Santner. Tossed up on off, Santner thumps it over the man at mid off and picks up a boundary to open his account.
Flatter this time and angling in from off, Santner blocks it out.
Floated up, around off, this is pushed away towards mid off.
Mitchell Santner is the new batter. 40 needed off 106 balls with four wickets in the bank.

OUT! LBW! Fifty and out for Tom Latham and Ireland are right back in it! Simi Singh delivers the arm ball, this one pitches on middle and just keeps on coming in with the angle. Latham is pushed onto the back foot as he looks to work it away. The ball skids on and pings Latham on the back pad. The finger is raised immediately after the appeal and Singh has the breakthrough. Surprisingly, there's no review from the skipper and he walks back in disappointment. The replay shows that it was a good decision not to review as the ball was hitting the leg stump.
SIX! Gorgeous timing on that and what a way to bring up his FIFTY! Tossed up around off, Tom Latham dances down the track and with utmost ease just lofts it over the mid-wicket fence for a maximum.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Tom Latham tries to play the sweep but gets a top edge and the ball goes over the fielder at short fine leg. They cross.
Bowls it full this time on middle, Michael Bracewell comes down the pitch and drives it to mid on for a run.
On middle, blocked out.
Tossed up on middle, Michael Bracewell defends off his front foot.
Floated on middle, Michael Bracewell blocks it to the off side.
Slower through the air outside off, Michael Bracewell opens the face of his bat and edges it past the man at second slip down to third man for a single.
Change in bowling. Andy McBrine (8-0-38-0) is back on.
Flatter this time, around off. Latham defends it out.
Well placed! Around middle, Tom Latham uses his feet to work it well in front of mid-wicket for an easy brace. 50 needed more.
Another direct hit but no harm is done. On a length and around off, Latham looks to bunt it towards point and steal a single but is sent back and rightly so.
Full and straight, this is driven straight back past the bowler for a single.
Nicely bowled! Simi Singh sees Tom Latham stepping out and floats it outside off, Latham ends up dragging it on the bounce to wide mid on, for a quick single.

TWO LEG BYES! Unnecessary from the fielder and they get an extra run. This is slowed up on a length and drifted onto the pads, Tom Latham looks to work it 'round the corner but gets it off the pads towards short fine leg. The batters get across for one but a wide throw at the batter's end allows them to come back for two.
Slower one, full and around off, Michael Bracewell plays late and pushes it towards point. 56 needed more.
In the area outside off, Michael Bracewell offers no shot.
Serves it close to off, a touch full, Bracewell is on the front foot as he blocks.
On a length around off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
FOUR! Pure timing! Fullish and outside off, Michael Bracewell creams his drive through extra cover and it races away on this lightning outfield for a boundary.
A gentle length delivery, in the channel outside off, Michael Bracewell has nothing to do with it.
Loopy and on middle, Latham skips down the track and flicks but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Fires it full and around off, Latham defends it to the cover region.
Too full and on off, Bracewell strokes it down to long off for one.
Flighted and around off, Bracewell is on the front foot as he defends it back.
Fuller and around middle, it's helped to square leg for one.
Quicker and shorter on off, defended from the back foot to mid-wicket.
Some movement off the pitch there. Around off, on a length, nipping away, Michael Bracewell feels for it and gets beaten.
On a length outside off, angling away, Michael defends it off his front foot.
FOUR! Tonk! Shot of a batter in prime form. Short in length, around middle and off, Bracewell camps back and pulls it powerfully through square leg for a boundary.
Drifting down the leg side, it's eased away through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
The hero from the last game, Michael Bracewell walks in at number 7.

OUT! CHOPS IT ON! The quickfire knock from Glenn Phillips comes to an end. Craig Young delivers it short and wide outside off, at 129.7 kph, Glenn Phillips stands tall inside the crease and tries to reach out for it. He attempts to slap it through the line but all he manages is a thick inside edge onto the stumps. Ireland are trying hard to stay in the hunt. Can they pick a few more wickets?
Back of a length around off, hitting the deck hard, Glenn Phillips defends it down from the back foot.
Craig Young (5-1-27-0) is brought back into the attack.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Latham is on the front foot as he blocks. 68 needed more off 138 balls.
Shortish and on middle, worked to deep mid-wicket for one.
A touch fuller and slower, around middle, Glenn flicks it to short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Goodness me, that's raw power. Flatter and shorter, around off, Glenn Phillips immediately drops his weight on the back leg and bludgeons it through extra cover.
Tossed up, around off, Glenn wrists it towards square leg.
Fuller and around off, Latham pushes it to the right of the cover fielder and picks up a single.
Flighted delivery, full and around off, Glenn Phillips calmly flicks it to short mid-wicket. 10 from the over.
Fuller and on middle, defended back from the crease.
Quicker and shorter outside off, Glenn punches it to covers.
SIX! If it's in the arc, it's out of the park. Loopy and full, around off and spinning in, Glenn Phillips kneels down and launches it over wide long on. He is straight away in the top gear.
Flatter and shorter around off, Glenn punches it to covers where Andy Balbirnie makes a fine stop.
FOUR! This is how Phillips bats. A long hop around off, turning in and there to be hit. Glenn Phillips camps back and powers his pull shot over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Shortish on off, punched down to long on for a single.
Around off, defended again.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Turning in from around off, Glenn Phillips goes back and keeps it out off the inner edge.
Glenn Phillips is the next man in.

OUT! RUN OUT! A direct hit from the deep and Ireland have a wicket against the run of play. You just cannot keep Curtis Campher out of the game. He keeps adding value to this team. Flighted and full, around off, Henry Nicholls goes down on one knee and sweeps it through square leg. They complete a single and try for the second run. Campher attacks the ball in the deep and hits the bull's eye at the striker's end as Nicholls dives in. They appeal and the umpire goes upstairs. The Irish players are celebrating already. The replays show that Nicholls is well short of the crease. 85 runs needed in 154 balls.

Is that run out? An absolute bullet of a throw from the deep and Curtis Campher has hit the stumps. This seems to be close and the decision is sent upstairs. The replay shows that Henry Nicholls is short of his crease and the decision on the big screen is OUT!
A touch short in length, around middle, Latham moves back and works it through square leg for an easy run.
Flatter and shorter on off, Henry goes on the back foot and defends it down safely.
Rocks back to a short ball and punches it towards mid on.
Flighted and around off, Nicholls eases down the track and bunts it to mid on.
Full and floated, around off, Henry lunges and defends it to the off side.
Goes on the back foot and slaps a short ball to deep point for a single.
Loopy and full, around off, Latham walks forward and defends it back.
Around middle, Henry goes deep inside the crease and keeps it out towards short mid-wicket.
Fires it in, short and on middle, Nicholls tucks it through mid-wicket and collects another brace.
Short again but this time outside off, Nicholls cuts it to deep point and returns for the second run.
Quicker and shorter on middle, Henry Nicholls moves back and helps it to mid-wicket.
Walks forward and pushes a full ball to mid on.
Flatter delivery, around off and skidding in, Henry goes on the back foot and defends it down.
Simi Singh to roll his arm now.
FOUR! Clinically done. Fuller in length, around middle and leg, Tom Latham goes down on one knee and unfurls a beautiful sweep shot behind square leg for a boundary. 7 from the over, 92 needed more.
On the pads, it's clipped to square leg for a run.

Edged but safe! Quicker and shorter, around off, Latham goes back to cut but gets a thick outside edge. It clips the thigh of the keeper and deflects past first slip for a run. This has happened for the second time now.
Senses the charge and pulls his length back a bit. It's outside off and Tom makes a late adjustment to keep it out safely towards point.
Slower through the air, full and around off, Latham leans forward and defends it to the off side.
Short in length and around off, Henry goes on the back foot and punches it through covers for a run.
Pitches it up and outside off, Nicholls drives it to the left of extra cover for a quick run.
Short and wide outside off, Henry Nicholls cuts but finds point.
FOUR! Finds the fence! Fuller in length, around middle and leg, Nicholls leans across and flicks it in front of square leg for a boundary. Below 100 needed now.
A touch short and outside off, Henry Nicholls goes on the back foot again and defends it towards mid off.
On a good length, around middle and off, Henry defends it from the back foot.
Fuller in length and outside off, Henry gets on the front foot and pushes it to cover-point.
Short and close to the off pole, Henry Nicholls rocks back and cuts it to the man at deep point for a run.
Goes full and slides it on the pads, Tom Latham gets down to sweep it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Around middle, this is worked 'round the corner for one more by Nicholls.
Shorter in length and a bit wider too, this is played off the back foot towards deep cover for a single.
Flatter this time, angling into middle and leg. Latham goes back and pushes it towards the bowler.

Appeal for an lbw from the bowler but it is turned down. This is a gem of a delivery from Andy McBrine, drifted into middle and the ball turns away after pitching. Tom Latham looks to defend but gets beaten and the ball goes off the back leg and past the keeper. They pick up a couple of leg byes.
This is on a length on middle and leg, Tom Latham misses his flick and gets hit on his thigh pad. The ball goes to the leg side and they get across for a leg bye.
A bit full outside off, Tom Latham pushes it but straight to short third man.
Full and outside off, Henry Nicholls knocks it to mid off for a quick single.
Back of length on off, Tom Latham punches it off his back foot through cover-point for another run.
Bowls it full and outside off, Henry Nicholls opens the face of his bat and guides to third man for a single.
Serves it on a length outside off, Henry Nicholls leaves it alone.
Around middle, this is worked away towards wide mid on for a quick single by Nicholls and he is off the mark.
Nicely looped up now and at the stumps, Nicholls just pushes it towards mid on.
Quicker and flatter, outside off. Henry Nicholls taps it towards cover-point.
Tosses it up now, around off, this is knocked down to long off for one.
Floated up on off stump, Latham presses forward to make the block.
This is fired in fuller and on off stump, Latham defends it out.

Drinks break. It's been a great recovery from New Zealand after losing two wickets in the blink of an eye. Although Finn Allen got dismissed on the last ball, he did an amazing job to pull New Zealand out of troubled waters with his attacking batting. Tom Latham is now set at the crease and his job will be to anchor this chase till the end. Ireland have not been able to build on a fantastic start and are on the back foot. They need wickets in a cluster to make a strong back. 116 needed more off 198 balls as Henry Nicholls walks in next.

OUT! CAUGHT! The man with the golden arm does it again! Curtis Campher goes full and angles it into middle and leg, Finn Allen looks to just loft it over the man at mid on but gets it off the toe end of the bat. The ball is chipped towards Josh Little and he makes no mistake inside the ring. A much-needed breakthrough then for Ireland and Allen departs after a fiery knock. 116 needed now off 33 overs.
Commentary.Howout: c Josh Little b Curtis Campher

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, angled into middle. Finn Allen gets behind the line of the ball to make the block.
Short of a good length, angling in from outside off, Latham guides it towards third man for an easy single.
FOUR! Well-timed and the 100-run partnership is up between these two! Back of a length again and around off, Latham plays it a bit late and caresses it behind point for a boundary.

Close call! Back of a length and outside off, Tom Latham mistimes the cut shot towards point and looks for the single. His partner sends him back as Harry Tector fires in a throw from the point region. Tector misses and if he had hit, Latham would have been struggling.
This is on middle, Allen works it away towards deep mid-wicket and rotates the strike.

TURN AND BOUNCE! This is slower through the air on off, drifting away. Tom Latham tries to play but gets an outside edge and hits the keeper on his knees. Luckily for Latham, it does not carry to the fielder at point.
Slightly shorter and on leg, Allen flicks it to square leg for one.
SIX! SMASHED! Andy McBrine bowls it full and outside off, Finn Allen slog-sweeps it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Flatter and on middle, Allen pushes it towards mid on.
Floated outside off, Allen defends it to the off side.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Allen knocks it to short mid-wicket.
Pulls back the length a fair bit and bowls it outside off, Tom Latham looks to cut off the back foot but finds the man at point.
A touch fuller this time around and around off, Latham presses forward and pushes it out towards extra cover.
Back to around the wicket for the left-hander and angles it in towards the off pole, Latham keeps it out.
Back of a length, around off, easily steered towards third man by Allen for one more.
WIDE! Campher tries to push it wide and force Finn Allen to fetch it but spills it beyond the tramline. A wide is called.
Length this time, around the top of off. Latham hangs back and just guides it down to third man for a single.
Campher pitches it up first up on off stump, Latham leans in and drives it straight towards mid off.
Curtis Campher, the man with the golden arm, is inserted into the attack.

Big appeal for LBW! This is full and on middle, Allen goes for the reverse sweep but misses and gets hit on his pads. The fielders appeal but the finger stays down. Ireland decide not to take the review.
Tossed up on off, Latham slices it past covers for one.
Short again outside off, turning in. Finn Allen forces it towards long on for a single.
A bit short outside off, Tom Latham punches it to sweeper cover for a run.

FIFTY! Finn Allen gets to his half century. This is floated on middle, Finn Allen flicks it past mid-wicket for a single. A lovely knock from the opener after a nervy start. He survived that phase and has looked fluent since then. Can he continue and score big here?
Tossed up on off, Tom Latham eases it towards long off for a single.
FOUR! Finn Allen seems to be in a hurry here and all of a sudden has moved to 49. This is fuller and on leg, Allen whips it away past the man at mid-wicket for a boundary.
Back of a length, around off, this is defended off the back foot by Allen.
Excellent running! On a shorter length and at the body, Latham hops back and dabs it down on the deck and races through for a quick single.
Little goes fuller and wider, the ball keeps a shade low as well. Latham looks to drive it through covers but misses.
Good length, angling into middle and leg, Tom Latham tucks it away neatly off his hips and through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
This is banged in short and over leg stump, Allen pulls it down to fine leg and collects a single.
Shorter in length and around off, this is punched off the back foot towards sweeper cover for one.

FOUR BYES! Through everyone! This is a bit quicker and flatter, turning in from around middle. Finn Allen rocks back looking to pull it away but it isn't that short. The ball turns in and goes agonizingly close past the leg stump and into the fine leg fence.
Slower through the air outside off, turning in. Allen blocks it to the off side.
Full and on middle, Allen uses his feet and works it to mid-wicket.
Wide! Tossed up on middle, turning down the leg side. Allen misses his flick. It is called a wide.
Floated on middle, Allen blocks it out.
Starts with a flatter and quicker delivery, drifting into the pads. Finn Allen tries to work it away but gets hit on his pads.
Time for some spin. Andy McBrine, the off spinner, comes into the attack. A leg slip is in place. The big frame of Paul Stirling is manning that area.
Back of a length, around off, Allen punches it off the back foot towards mid on for one.
Goes fuller this time, around off. Latham presses forward and caresses it towards backward point. The call is of no but a slight fumble by the fielder allows the batters to sneak in a run.
Keeps it short and bowls it around off, Finn Allen with a swivel-pull down to deep backward square leg for a single.
Leg bye! Little angles this one into the body, Latham tries to fend it away but misses and the ball goes off the pads towards backward square leg. They get a leg bye.
This time on the other side! Short and wide, this is cut away through the point region for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Josh Little is greeted with a boundary! Starts off with a loosener, shorter and on middle, Tom Latham rocks back and pulls it hard and behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
The umpire signals the start of Powerplay 2! The fielding side can now have up to 4 fielders outside the inner ring till the 40th over.
Short in length and outside off, Allen goes on the back foot and taps it down to cover-point.  At the end of Powerplay 1, New Zealand are 56 for 2.
FOUR! No stopping this one! Back of a length, around off, Finn Allen eases himself on the back foot and packs a punch through covers for a boundary. Boom.
Mistimed shot! Fuller in length outside off, Allen tries to fire it over extra cover but ends up slicing it behind backward point. The ball lands safely in the deep and they get two runs.
Hurls across a length ball outside off, Allen shoulders arms.
Full and wide outside off, Allen tries to hammer it through the line but it takes the inner edge and runs towards mid on. A good diving stop inside the ring.
Shortish and on off, Allen stays back and plays it down on the off side. Not in the gap.
Short again, around middle, this time it has been pulled to long leg for a single. 20 from the over. 50 comes up for New Zealand.
FOUR! It's raining boundaries from the bat of Finn Allen. Adair overcorrects his length. Bangs it in short and around leg, Allen swivels and pulls it down to fine leg for a boundary.
FOUR! Finn Allen is in top gear. His attack has put off the bowler. A low full toss around off, Allen just shows the full face of his bat and caresses it through mid off for a boundary.
FOUR! Fires a gunshot this time. Fuller again, outside off, Finn drills his drive through extra cover and it hurries away to the fence.
SIX! This is an enormous hit! Finn Allen has decided to attack now. Fuller in length and wide outside off, Allen flexes his muscles and dismisses it over long off for a maximum.
Shortish and angling down the leg side, Latham tries to pull but doesn't middle his shot. It takes the inner edge and goes to fine leg. The batters cross.
Around off, on a good length, Allen defends it from the crease. 10 from the over.
SIX! All the way! A little too full and around off, Finn Allen finds it in his zone and powers it all the way over long off for a maximum.
On middle, defended from the back foot.
Full again, around off, Allen gets close to the line of the delivery and bunts it down to mid on.
Good reply from the bowler. Bowls it full and outside off, holding its line, Allen does well to let it go. Craig Young should look to make him drive rather than testing him with the short ball.
FOUR! Finn Allen is opening his arms now. Fractionally short in length, around off, Allen turns inside the crease and pulls it powerfully to the deep square leg fence.
Very full this time, around off, Finn pushes it firmly to covers where the fielder fumbles slightly and they get a single.

Fuller in length and outside off, Latham gets on the front foot and drives it through extra cover. Curtis Campher moves across to his right from mid off and puts in a dive to stop the racing ball. The batters get only a run.
Fraction short, around off, Latham goes back and tries to steer it past point. Harry Tector though makes a diving stop.
Mark Adair is mixing his length here. Goes short and around off, Allen stays back and pulls it down to long leg for one.
A near-yorker around off, Finn Allen does well to keep it out safely.
Swing and a miss! Adair offers width outside off and Finn throws his bat at it but only to get beaten. The bowler stares at the batter.
Fuller in length and outside off, once again Latham strokes off the front foot but finds wide mid off.
Too full this time, on off, Latham pushes it with good timing but straight to wide mid off.
Craig pitches it just ahead of a good length, outside off, Latham gets on the front foot and defends.
Serves it on a good length around off, Latham defends it from the back foot to the off side.
Drifting down the leg side, Finn helps it off his pads to deep backward square leg. They cross.
Young bowls it short and outside off, Allen mistimes his shot back towards the bowler.
Almost drags it on. Short in length and outside off, Allen tries to turn and pull but it takes the bottom edge and beats the stumps by a whisker. The keeper fumbles and they cross for a run.
Fullish around leg, angling down, Allen walks across the stumps, trying to flick but misses. It takes his pads and goes to the keeper.
Wide! Adair bowls it quite wide outside off, from over the wicket, Allen makes a leave.
Fuller and on off, holding its line from there, Latham closes the face of his bat early as he attempts to flick. The ball takes the leading edge and scoots through backward point for a run.
Extra bounce this time. It lands on a length around off and shoots up. Latham tries to flick but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.
Angling in, from a length around off, Latham tries to flick but misses. It takes his thigh pad and rolls towards the cover region.
Adair continues his spell from 'round the wicket. Lands it on a good length around off, Latham sits on the back foot and defends it down.
Maiden! Back of a length, around off, Finn goes on his toes and pushes it defensively to covers. Excellent comeback by Craig after conceding 10 runs in his first over.
Fuller on off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Delivers it on a length and around off, Finn defends it from the back foot to the off side. Allen is known for his attacking batting but he has been kept quiet so far.
Inswinger on this occasion, on a fuller length around off, Finn Allen is solidly behind the line as he blocks.
A touch too straight this time, around middle, Finn defends it on the leg side.
Unplayable! That's a gem. Craig Young serves it on a fuller length around off, Finn Allen is forced to play the line but it nips away a wee bit to beat the outside edge.
In the channel outside off, Tom has nothing to do with it. Excellent over by Adair again.
Fuller and on off, shaping away a bit, Latham plays at it from the outer half of his blade as it rolls to cover-point.
Around off, on a good length, Latham defends it from the back foot.
Beauty! Adair putting the 'round the wicket angle to use. He puts it on a length around off, Latham tries to play the angle but gets beaten by the away movement. Two slips waiting for any edge.

Adair switches to around the wicket and bowls it on a shortish length outside off, Latham covers the line and shoulders arms. This angle troubled Tom during the Test series in England where Broad had him at sea.
Fuller in length on middle, no movement there, Allen helps it in the gap at mid-wicket for an easy run.
On a good length outside off, angling away, Latham defends it from the back foot to the off side. 10 from the over, New Zealand trying to recover after early blows.

Young feeds it on a good length, around off and gets it to straighten from there. Finn stays back to work it on the leg side but gets a leading edge. It runs down to third man and Allen opens his account with a single.
The line is straight this time, Tom tucks it behind square leg for a run.
FOUR! The New Zealand skipper is dealing in boundaries at the moment. Back of a length, around off, Tom Latham goes on the back foot and punches it sweetly through point.
Fuller again, around off, Latham plays yet another well-timed drive but finds the wide mid off fielder.
FOUR! Beautiful shot! Craig Young goes searching for swing and overpitches in the process. It's outside off and Latham plays a crunchy drive through cover-point for a boundary.
Lands it on a length and outside off, getting it to go straight on, Finn leaves. End of a stupendous first over by Adair.
Craig Young to start from the opposite end.
Wide! Mark Adair fails to control his line this time. Slips a length ball down the leg side, swinging further down, Allen tries to flick but misses.
Hurls a length ball in the zone outside off, Finn Allen makes a watchful leave.
Fuller in length and outside off, Latham drives it without much timing but the ball goes in the gap at extra cover. They cross.
No hat-trick. Back of a length, in the channel outside off, Tom Latham drops his wrists and allows it through to the keeper.
The Kiwi skipper, Tom Latham walks out with his side in a fix early in the innings.

OUT! SOUND OF TIMBER! Mark Adair is on fire, he has two in two. This time it's not a yorker but very full around off. Will Young tries to defend without any footwork but misses as the ball nips back in to beat the inside edge. The stumps are shattered. The crowd is going wild. Adair on a hat-trick...
Will Young is in at number 3.

OUT! BOWLED! Martin Guptill bags a golden duck. What a start from Mark Adair! He nails his yorker to perfection. Speeds in from over the wicket, eyes the blockhole straight away and attempts to catch the batter unaware. Martin Guptill's feet go nowhere, his bat comes down late and the ball goes behind to floor the stumps. Mark Adair jumps in delight!
